caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1650 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr. Ruhul Amin, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Abdul Hye Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Mr Hefazul Bari, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Khalfa Shamsun Arahar, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent Nos. 1 and 5
parties:
Md. Numan Ali -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC), represented by its Chairman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 8. Mr. Ruhul Amin, the learned. Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in rejecting the review petition is misconceived on the ground of law and facts as because the High Court Division failed to consider the scope of review of a judgment within the meaning of order 41 read with section 144 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He further submits that the High Court Division also failed to consider following the Guideline for review delivered by this Division in case of Seraj Uddin and others Vs. Saiful Alam reported in 56 DLR (AD) 41 and thus, this has resulted the erroneous impugned judgment. He finally submits that the High Court Division also failed to consider the fact that in a similar situation large number employees of BADC obtained arrear salary and other service benefits pursuant to the judgment delivered by the same Bench (under review) and judgment delivered by different Bench of the High Court Division and therefore, a discriminatory situation has been created which calls for an interference by way of review and thus, this has resulted the erroneous impugned judgment. Hence, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside for the ends of justice.
